events.label: US Market Holiday — Independence Day observed (July 4 falls on Saturday)
events.note: US equity markets closed Friday July 3. 3-day weekend gap (July 3–6). June NFP printed 57K on July 2 (vs. 110K consensus; -74K net revisions to April-May) — growth-scare scenario. Any repricing accumulates over the full gap before July 7 open. QQQ July 18 puts are the only active hedges through the gap.

events.label: SPCX added to Nasdaq-100 (~$7.3B forced passive inflows: $4.3B QQQ/QQQM + $3B Russell); post-57K NFP holiday return
events.note: Dual catalyst day: (1) SPCX Nasdaq-100 inclusion effective July 7 — QQQ/QQQM forced to buy ~$4.3B of SPCX at index weight; $3B Russell reweighting adds; $7.3B total mechanical demand regardless of macro conditions. (2) July 7 open reflects full repricing of 57K NFP growth scare (vs. 110K consensus) over 3-day July 4 gap. SPX closed July 2 at ~7,453 (7 points below 7,460 regime floor); VIX 16.81 (held below 17). For dual-gate Day 1 restart: SPX must close >7,460 AND VIX <17 on July 7. NVDA must close above $200 with above-average volume for full re-entry. SPCX entry improved from $163 pre-market to ~$156 close on July 2. 57K NFP: July 28 FOMC hike probability collapsed to ~19.4% from 33% — rate-relief tailwind for July 7 open.

events.label: FOMC Minutes from June 17 meeting (est. ~2 PM ET) — first post-dot-plot-removal release
events.note: Minutes from the June 17 FOMC meeting (est. release ~3 weeks after). First FOMC at which Warsh removed the dot plot. Context has shifted materially: 57K NFP (July 2) versus the June 17 committee's data backdrop. July 28 hike probability ~19.4% (down from 33% pre-NFP). Hawkish minutes (inflation focus, 3-hike path supported) = July 28 probability bounces back toward 25–30%. Dovish tone (data dependence, growth concern noted) = September rate-cut pricing accelerates. ISM June 53.3, Prices Paid 73.0, WTI -30% Q2 are the post-June-17 data the committee did not have. SK Hynix ADR listing expected around this date — first US capital-markets clearing of HBM4 demand thesis; positive read-through for TSM, AVGO, NVDA.

events.label: SK Hynix ADR Nasdaq listing — $29.4B offering, 17.79M shares
events.note: SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR listing — $29.4B offering (17.79M shares). Underwriters: BofA, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, JPMorgan. Context: Korea circuit breaker session July 2 (KOSPI -4.45%, SK Hynix -10.96%) on Apple/CXMT/YMTC mobile DRAM narrative — separate from HBM4 (AI), but created sentiment overhang on the Korean semiconductor complex. ADR listing at/above $29.4B offering price = institutional vote of confidence in HBM4 demand thesis; below = circuit-breaker narrative confirmed as a broader HBM4 concern. TSM and NVDA read-through constructive if ADR prices above consensus. Underwriter stabilization mandate provides ADR floor.

events.label: June CPI release (est. 8:30 AM ET) — regime-defining event for summer; 57K NFP makes CPI the summer's most important data
events.note: June CPI is now the regime-defining event following 57K NFP (July 2). With rate cuts back on the table for 2026 (July 28 hike probability ~19.4%) and growth-scare pricing in equities, CPI determines whether the regime is 'rate cuts + growth recovery' (bullish) or 'sticky inflation + slowing growth' (stagflation — worst multiple environment). Input-cost context: ISM Prices Paid 73.0 from 82.1 in May (9.1-point drop); WTI at $66.50 (-30%+ Q2 — largest quarterly decline since 2020); June CPI captures first full month of Iranian oil normalization. Scenario A: CPI ≤3.5% — rate cuts for 2026 confirmed, BofA 3-hike framework withdrawn, BUY upgrades to HIGH conviction for full earnings season. Scenario B: CPI 4.0%+ — stagflation risk; STEP ASIDE or BEARISH warranted even with weak NFP.

events.label: TSLA Q2 2026 earnings (est.) — after market close; 480K delivery beat sets the floor
events.note: Q2 earnings follow the July 2 delivery report: 480,126 vehicles delivered (vs. 406,024 consensus; +25% YoY; best-ever Q2). Despite the blowout beat, TSLA fell ~7.49% on July 2 (sell-the-news + growth scare). Q2 earnings call (~July 22) is the fundamental clearing event: need gross margin recovery (>25%), FSD revenue recognition at scale, and Q3 delivery guide >450K for the stock to re-rate above $420. Weak gross margin (<22%) or no FSD clarity = $393 July 2 close is the near-term top. The delivery beat is confirmed; the financial execution is not yet validated.

events.label: FOMC meeting (July 28-29) — hike probability ~19.4% after 57K NFP; June CPI (~Jul 14) is the determining input
events.note: July 28 FOMC hike probability collapsed from 33% (Warsh's Sintra hawkishness) to ~19.4% after 57K NFP (July 2). Policymakers expected to hold while monitoring CPI trajectory. June CPI (~July 14) is the primary input: CPI ≤3.5% = hike probability collapses further, rate cuts discussed; CPI 4.0%+ = September hike back on the table. Nine of 18 officials projected at least one 2026 hike at June 17 meeting; 57K NFP shifts that calculus toward a pause. SCOTUS upheld Fed independence June 29 — Warsh can move in either direction without political pressure.

events.label: META Q2 2026 earnings — AI cloud business first quantification; earnings season peak week
events.note: Bloomberg reported July 1 that Meta is building an AI cloud business to sell excess compute capacity (META surged +8.88%). META gave back -4.81% on July 2 to $583.50 (now at the $575–595 'better entry' zone). Q2 earnings July 29 is the first event where management must quantify the cloud business timeline, revenue model, and go-to-market plan. The July 2 NFP-driven rate-relief narrative (rate cuts for 2026 back on the table) is actually META-positive: lower discount rates expand the multiple for a $60B+ annual FCF machine with a new cloud revenue stream. GOOGL, MSFT, and AMZN also report in mid-to-late July — peak Q3 earnings risk window.

events.label: Iran-US Islamabad Declaration 60-day deadline — Hormuz full reopening + sanctions relief
events.note: Deal operational from June 18 MOU signing; 60-day window expires August 13. WTI fell to $66.50 on July 2 (4.25-month low; -30%+ Q2, largest quarterly decline since 2020) — oil normalization is proceeding ahead of the original MOU schedule. If August 13 deadline met with full Hormuz clearance and confirmed sanctions relief, WTI could extend to $62–65. Failure or reversal = oil spike reversal and energy re-rally; Brent trigger returns to focus ($97 threshold). Current Brent ~$69.50 = $27.50 buffer; risk is asymmetric to the downside for oil prices.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — $91B revenue guide; AI capex cycle fundamental clearing event
events.note: NVDA's Q2 FY27 earnings is the fundamental clearing event for the AI capex thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. NVDA has failed the $200 re-entry gate for three consecutive sessions (July 2 close: $194.84); Korea circuit breaker (SK Hynix -10.96%) extended AI semiconductor distribution. The $200 gate failure means the July 7 post-SPCX attempt is the next gate test; August 26 earnings remains the ultimate fundamental clearing event. Any Q2 deceleration in the guide vs. $91B challenges the entire 2026 AI-infrastructure re-rating. TSM, AMD, AVGO all read-through from NVDA earnings.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since the June 12 IPO. SPCX confirmed in Russell 1000 and Nasdaq-100 (effective July 7). Capital structure: $75B IPO + $60B xAI acquisition + $20B bond offering = $155B in obligations. First earnings (Starlink subscriber/ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn rate) is the fundamental clearing event. Two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume required before re-entry; SPCX closed July 2 at ~$156.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs; the $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang on top. Exact date pending the prospectus's stated terms.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories. Monitor for filing date announcement as a potential AI sentiment catalyst. Date is approximate placeholder for H1 2027 window.
